question: Should OpenClaw core add native cross-gateway session messaging, and what peer identity, authorization, replay/idempotency, delivery, transcript-ownership, and config contract should it use?
rationale: The requested behavior crosses gateway, session-state, message-delivery, credential, and operator-scope boundaries, so automation cannot safely choose the permanent API or security model.

options.title: Design the contract first
options.body: Keep this issue open as the concrete session-tool tracker while maintainers define the peer trust, scope, delivery, transcript, and upgrade semantics before code lands.

options.title: Sponsor a fresh narrow implementation
options.body: Invite a new implementation only after the stale PR's proof, idempotency, URL-policy, and allowlist concerns are resolved in a maintainer-approved shape.

options.title: Defer native core support
options.body: Document plugin, MCP, channel, or operator-run workarounds if maintainers decide not to add core cross-gateway session routing now.

recommendation.title: Design the contract first
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open as the concrete session-tool tracker while maintainers define the peer trust, scope, delivery, transcript, and upgrade semantics before code lands.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest combined history signal across the session-tool implementation, Gateway URL-policy boundary, and the maintainer decision to keep this issue canonical after closing the stale PR.
